title: Instagram hashtags
lede: Hashtags are the # labels Instagram has supported since 2011. Instagram says they tell it what a post is about but add no reach by themselves, and since December 2025 caps them at five; marketing studies still measure small reach gains from the right count.

sections.heading: Does a hashtag add reach
sections.body: Instagram's answer is no, not by itself. In 2025 Adam Mosseri, the head of Instagram, said hashtags "don't work" to increase reach [1], and that they are "a great way to let people know what a post is about and connect posts" [2]. Instagram's ranking explainer lists what orders Feed, roughly by importance: first your own activity, then information about the post, such as how many people have liked it and how quickly [3][4]. Explore groups posts by who engages with them, "without us necessarily understanding what each post is about" [5]. Where a hashtag does count is search: Meta says Instagram scores a hashtag result partly on how closely the words of a search match the words in the hashtag [6].

sections.heading: What the studies say
sections.body: Studies by marketing-software companies disagree with each other more than with Instagram. Later looked at 18.1 million feed posts published through its own tool and found reach rising with hashtag count: 20 hashtags had the highest average reach rate, with 30 close behind [1][2]. Fanpage Karma's 1.6 million posts point the other way past five: 5 hashtags reached 2% more than none, 1 to 3 did slightly worse than none, and more than 5 lost 3% [3][4]. Hootsuite's 2021 test on one account, 20 posts, found 3 to 5 hashtags averaged a reach of 462 against 394 for 30, and called itself "certainly not definitive" [5][6]. Fanpage Karma words its own result as a correlation, with an effect on reach that is "small but clearly measurable" [7].

sections.heading: What changed
sections.body: Instagram added hashtags in January 2011, to help people discover photos and each other [1]. In December 2017 it let people follow a hashtag [2]. Since then it has pulled back step by step. It removed the "Recent" tab from hashtag pages for a while on October 30, 2020, to slow misinformation around the U.S. presidential election [3], and in April 2023 it removed searching recent hashtag posts for good, leaving a curated selection of popular ones [4]. Following hashtags ended on December 13, 2024 [5]. In December 2025 Instagram began cutting the number of hashtags a post or reel caption can carry to five [6].

sections.heading: How many to use
sections.body: For years a post could carry up to 30 hashtags, and in 2021 Instagram's @creators account advised using only 3 to 5 [1][2]. In December 2025 the advice became a rule. Instagram said it "will gradually update the number of hashtags that you can include in a caption for a reel or post to five", because "using fewer (up to 5) more targeted hashtags, rather than many generic ones, can improve both your content's performance and people's experience" [3][4]. Later's 2026 guide adds that the cap counts tags in the caption and the comments together, so moving some into a comment buys no extra slots [5]. Hootsuite's own advice is 3 to 5 [6].

sections.heading: What a founder should do
sections.body: Treat a hashtag as a label and the post as the product. Instagram's ranking starts from what viewers do, then how many people like a post and how quickly [1][2]. Hashtags still feed search, where the words people type are matched against them [3]. So the sources agree on a short routine: use up to five tags [4], make them specific to what the post is about rather than generic words like "photo" [5], and check what works for your own account, since the studies do not agree on the best count [6][7][8].

fights.body: Marketers' own data says hashtags still move reach, if modestly. Fanpage Karma analyzed 1.6 million posts and found that "posts with 5 hashtags achieve the greatest reach (+2% compared to posts without any hashtags)" [1]. Its 2026 update says "the use of hashtags continues to correlate with better performance. The impact on reach is small but clearly measurable" [2]. Later, across 18.1 million feed posts, found that "posts with 20 hashtags receive the highest average reach rate" [3]. Hootsuite's 2021 test saw posts with hashtags reach more people than the same account's earlier posts without any [4]. Instagram calls a hashtag a label; these studies measure that label in reach.

fights.note: Instagram's own words are about intent; the studies measure outcomes, and they find a small positive effect.

backers.note: Quotes check out on all four pages; the effect is small but it is what the data shows.

fights.body: Use all five. Fanpage Karma's 1.6 million posts show 1 to 3 hashtags doing slightly worse than none, and the best reach at 5, then 4 [1]. Its 2026 advice is plain: "for maximum visibility, it is therefore worth consistently using the 5 available hashtag slots" [2]. Read that way, Instagram's "up to 5" is a number to reach, not a range to stay inside [3].
